cases.title: Velocity at release point C is the reverse of the forward velocity
cases.note: released v is bit-exact -(history velocity at cursor+1): one damping step (x1.00896) above the velocity stored at the return point

cases.title: Playback order D->C->B->A, old history not deleted

observed.note_doubleBack: the frozen track contains B->C once as the first traversal and again as the recorded reversal, so the physical path is A..B..C..B..C..D

cases.note: playback = exact reverse of the frozen snapshot; history is strictly append-only (prefix bit-identical)

cases.title: Rewinding cue ball never leaves its history; the object ball is pushed and continues
cases.note: cue deviation is exactly 0 px on every rewound step including overlap steps; the object ball is pushed along the contact normal

cases.title: A potted object ball stays potted through repeated rewinds
cases.note: rails() is never called for a pocketed ball; the counter/flag are monotone

cases.title: A pocketed cue ball returns to the table when R is pressed
cases.note: every rewound step forces pocketed=false; a full rewind always parks the cue ball back on its history[0] = (292,280)

cases.title: Vertical rail bounce multiplies speed by exactly 1.5
cases.note: amplification is exactly 1.5x on the damped arrival speed (1.48668x on the previous step speed)

cases.title: Oblique rail bounce reflects correctly and scales the whole vector by 1.5
cases.note: both the tangential and the normal component are multiplied by exactly 1.5

cases.title: Simultaneous two-wall frame applies only one x1.5 (sub-clause)

observed.conclusion: a ball can never be clamped by two rails without being potted first -> the single-factor branch for simultaneous wall contact is dead code

cases.note: geometrically unreachable: the two-wall contact point is hypot(R,R)=17.25 px from the corner pocket centre, inside the 24 px capture radius, and inPocket() runs before the clamps

cases.title: Rewinding across an old rail-bounce point gives no second x1.5
cases.note: no rail code runs for a reverse ball; the traversal speed derived from the clamped position delta is only ~2/3 of the velocity stored at that entry

cases.title: All ten object balls potted shows the clear result; reset restores the initial state
cases.note: win check lives in rails(); it also force-ends an in-flight rewind and blocks further rewinds

cases.title: Long session: no script error, no position corruption, no tunnelling
cases.note: 600 simulated seconds of scripted play: no NaN, no out-of-bounds frame, no exception; render stays sub-ms

probes.title: Rail boost x1.5 long-term stability: unstable fixed point and speed blow-up

observed.boostMapExact: v_{n+1} = 1.5 * (v_n - 1.07*L)   (speed loss over a flight of L px is exactly 1.07*L)
observed.reachableByPlayer: a single legal full-power shot straight down the table (angle 90) diverges: the first flight is only 204.8 px, threshold 3.21*204.8 = 657 < 1258

probes.note: above 3.21*L the bounce map grows exponentially; positions stay clamped but the velocity reaches Infinity and coordinates become NaN

probes.title: Can wall-pinning farm unlimited energy? 96 configurations x 20 s
probes.note: no configuration beat the normal boost equilibrium; pinning does not farm energy

probes.title: Discrete collision (no CCD, STEP=1/120) head-on tunnelling sweep

observed.analyticNote: head-on: a miss needs one step to jump the whole 2R band, v > 4R/dt = 5856 px/s

probes.note: above 5856 px/s an exact head-on contact can be skipped; near-grazes fail far earlier (see D13)

probes.title: record() gate / entry spacing / rewind teleport / creep at rest

regressions.title: One legal max-power shot must not blow up ball state (finite, below 1e5 px/s)

observed.invariant: every ball coordinate and speed stays finite and below 1e5 px/s for 20 s after any legal input

regressions.note: the x1.5 rail boost has an unstable fixed point (v > 3.21*L): the short-axis flight grows without bound

regressions.title: Simulated time must never exceed real time (low FPS = slow motion, not catch-up)

regressions.title: A ball can never rest inside a pocket capture circle without being potted
